evals.prompt: hey, my sales dashboard (app.R, with sales.csv) is driving me crazy — it takes like 15+ seconds to be usable when I open it, and then every time I move the year slider everything flashes and takes forever again. a coworker mentioned something about 'the reactive graph' but I have no idea. Can you figure out what's making it slow and fix it? Please don't change what the app does — same charts, same filters, just faster.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that identifies the planted problems (per-session CSV read, duplicate filtering across outputs, no req() gating, renderUI churn, all outputs computing at startup, uncached slow reactive, no debounce) and targeted fixes that preserve app behavior. The agent should measure before/after (profvis or timing) rather than blindly refactoring, and should not rewrite the app from scratch.

assertions.text: changes-actually-applied: outputs/app/app.R differs meaningfully from the original fixture app.R (a real diff with performance edits), not just a copy

app-boots-and-renders: app.R parses, the app starts and serves HTTP 200, and at least one output renders without a server-side error (verify via shinytest2/chromote page visit or error-free boot log while a client loads; an index-page curl alone is NOT sufficient)
data-loaded-outside-server: sales.csv is no longer read inside server() — loading moved to global scope (a faster reader is acceptable if used at global scope)
single-shared-filter: the duplicated per-output filtering is consolidated so the expensive derivation is computed once per change (shared reactive consumed by multiple outputs)
req-gating-added: expensive outputs are guarded with req() (or equivalent) so they do not compute before inputs are ready/valid
renderui-replaced-or-justified: the city filter no longer rebuilds via renderUI/selectInput-in-uiOutput, OR the report explicitly justifies keeping it
slow-reactive-no-longer-refires: the Sys.sleep(1.5) benchmark reactive is no longer re-executed on every filter/slider change (cached, hoisted to constant data, or made event-driven)

behavior-preserved: all seven original outputs still exist (revenue_plot, revenue_summary, top_products, category_mix, store_scatter, benchmark_plot, detail_table) with the same UI structure and filters; any user-visible change is explicitly flagged in report.md

measurement-evidence-with-artifacts: report.md cites concrete before/after measurements AND the measurement artifacts (scripts, profvis output, timed logs) are saved under outputs/ (e.g. outputs/measurements/), not only in /tmp

evals.prompt: We rolled our model explorer app out to the team (about 10 people use it at various times, sometimes 4-5 at once) and it's been a disaster. When someone clicks 'Fit model' the entire app freezes for everyone — even the little clock in the corner stops updating. It was totally fine when just I used it during development. We can't get more server resources; what can we change in the app itself?
evals.expected_output: The agent should recognize the multi-user blocking symptom (long synchronous eventReactive blocking the R process), and fix it with ExtendedTask + future_promise (or mirai) + the existing task button, moving data loading out of server(), and de-duplicating the outputs that each call fit() independently. The clock output should keep ticking during fits. Should not reach for async before noting the duplicated-computation fixes.

assertions.text: changes-actually-applied: outputs/app/app.R differs meaningfully from the original fixture app.R (a real diff with performance edits), not just a copy

app-boots-and-renders: app.R parses, the app starts and serves HTTP 200, and at least one output renders without a server-side error (verify via shinytest2/chromote page visit or error-free boot log while a client loads; an index-page curl alone is NOT sufficient)

blocking-fit-moved-off-main-process: the simulated 4-second fit no longer runs synchronously in an eventReactive on the main R process — converted to ExtendedTask with future_promise/mirai (or an equivalent promises-based pattern); a body that runs synchronously inside ExtendedTask$new without a promise FAILS this
worker-backend-declared-at-top-level: future::plan(multisession) (or mirai::daemons) is configured at app top level, not omitted or set to sequential
no-reactive-reads-inside-worker: the task function receives values as arguments; no input$ or reactive reads inside the promise/worker body
task-button-still-wired: the existing input_task_button remains functional and wired to task state (bind_task_button or equivalent)
data-loaded-outside-server: survey.csv is no longer read inside server()
fit-consumed-once: the four outputs no longer each trigger/consume the fit independently in a way that re-runs work (a single shared consumer of the task result)
clock-keeps-ticking: the clock output continues updating while a fit runs (demonstrated by a test or argued correctly from the async semantics)

measurement-evidence-with-artifacts: report.md cites concrete evidence for the diagnosis and expected effect of changes AND measurement/verification artifacts are saved under outputs/, not only in /tmp

evals.prompt: I've been told my dashboard is 'doing too much work' but I can't tell where the time actually goes. Can you profile it properly, tell me the top 3 things making it slow, and fix the ones that can be fixed without changing the app's behavior or its design? I want to see before/after numbers.
evals.expected_output: The agent should run an actual profile (profvis and/or reactlog, plus bench::mark for A/B comparisons), report a prioritized diagnosis with concrete evidence, then apply a small number of targeted fixes, and report before/after measurements for at least the headline problem.

assertions.text: profiling-tool-actually-used: report shows evidence a real profiling/measurement tool ran (profvis summary, reactlog observations, bench::mark output, or timed measurements) — not purely static reasoning
ranked-top3-with-evidence: report explicitly ranks the top 3 performance problems with supporting evidence for each

diagnosis-matches-ground-truth: the diagnosis gets the reactive semantics right — the benchmark reactive (Sys.sleep 1.5s) reads NO reactive values so it runs once per session and blocks the first flush, NOT 're-runs on every input change'; and duplicate per-output filtering is correctly identified as repeated work
fixes-target-diagnosed-problems: applied fixes correspond to the diagnosed top problems; no wholesale rewrite (changes stay targeted and behavior-preserving)

before-after-numbers-consistent: at least one concrete before/after measurement for the headline problem, with units, internally consistent (the arithmetic reconciles; claimed deltas match the cited before/after values)
measurement-artifacts-saved: the measurement artifacts (scripts, profvis/bench output, timing logs) are saved under outputs/ (e.g. outputs/measurements/), not only in /tmp

app-boots-and-renders: app.R parses, the app starts and serves HTTP 200, and at least one output renders without a server-side error (verify via shinytest2/chromote page visit or error-free boot log while a client loads; an index-page curl alone is NOT sufficient)

behavior-preserved: all seven original outputs still exist (revenue_plot, revenue_summary, top_products, category_mix, store_scatter, benchmark_plot, detail_table) with the same UI structure and filters; any user-visible change is explicitly flagged in report.md
